issues.evidence: adjudicate: detected['safety'] needs only some alarm at or after onset, with no early alarms. The final post (marker) sample counts as such an alarm.
issues.required_action: Credit safety only for alarms on ordinary (non-marker) samples at or after onset, or report marker-only credit separately. Otherwise an end-only completion alarm counts as safety detection (category overlap).

issues.evidence: adjudicate: input_completion = complete and end in alarms. It ignores earlier alarms and which slot or category fired. response_completion uses the same end alarm, so one end alarm can credit both categories.
issues.required_action: Apply the same rule as response_completion (no earlier alarm), or report early alarms. State explicitly that the end alarm is not attributed to a category, or map slots to categories before scoring.

issues.evidence: witness: prefix=rows[:alarm_state], but the candidate alarm is at pre(alarm_state). The reference never judges pre(alarm_state). That is equivalent to post(alarm_state-1) only if no output depends combinationally on cycle-alarm_state inputs; s_ready may, and stability context depends on the ready values of that row.
issues.required_action: Label the PASS classification 'reference_PASS_on_prefix_through_post(alarm_state-1)', not 'candidate_false_alarm', unless pre(alarm_state) equality with post(alarm_state-1) is verified on the meaningful pins. Alternatively, have a separate Claude author add a pre-only adjudication path.

issues.evidence: witness: the 'reference_confirmed_DUT_violation' classification does not check that the reference failure matches the sample or category of the candidate alarm.
issues.required_action: Record the reference failure cycle, phase and category, and claim confirmation only when they match the candidate alarm.

issues.evidence: Reference FAIL with unknown records: the scorer uses fully_resolved separately, but observable_types counts any oracle FAIL.
issues.required_action: Report the oracle_unknown co-presence per type so FAIL plus unknown is never presented as resolved.

limitations: Oracle review from the specification found it consistent on these points: no-bypass pre/post basis; spurious or premature presented valid with ready=0 caught by sample(); a later reset does not erase failures; reset_clear checked on post; pre samples while rst=1 skipped; initial pre excluded; X/Z yields unknown without erasing failures; padding unknown before completion; truncation end waits; response debts are end-only; short tail yields UNRESOLVED.
Once an earlier failure or unknown sets the ld/lh flags, later presented-valid checks for that channel are suppressed until reset. Detection counts therefore reflect first violations only.
An incomplete accepted input frame at the end is a definite failure only if the scoreboard is known (li false).
No B/C sources, hidden traces or scores were reviewed. Physical coverage, synthetic controls and formal projections remain distinct.
Any oracle change requires a separate Claude author.
scope: The frozen-v2 check_rows is reused unchanged as the independent oracle for physical rows: development uses require_drained=true,min_tail=32 and final uses require_drained=true,min_tail=128. Final-post completion is judged on the last row's post sample, which matches the trace_done=1 sample without an extra edge. Safety-projection witnesses (trace_done=0) are for prefix adjudication only and prove no finite completion or end-only activation. Scores are definite detections with unknown context kept separate; they are not full PASS or soundness claims.
